left: select max(a+1+2) from t;
right: select max(a+3) from t;
label: equivalent
note: Integer addition regrouped (with a float column (a+1)+2 and a+3 can round differently).

left: select max(a+(1+2)) from t;
right: select max(a+3) from t;
label: equivalent

left: select * from t where a=1+2;
right: select * from t where a=3;
label: equivalent

left: select * from t where a+1=2;
right: select * from t where a=1;
label: equivalent
note: Integer a.

left: select 1 >= 3;
right: select false;
label: equivalent
note: int4ge is PostgreSQL's internal int4 >= function; scored as 1 >= 3.

left: select * from t where ((a>0 and b>0) and (c>0 and d>0));
right: select * from t where (a>0 and b>0 and c>0 and d>0);
label: equivalent

left: select * from t where 1=2;
right: select * from t where false;
label: equivalent

left: select * from t where 1=1;
right: select * from t where true;
label: equivalent

left: select * from t where a>10 and b=6 and a>2;
right: select * from t where a>10 and b=6;
label: equivalent
note: a > 10 implies a > 2.

left: select * from t where a>(10,2*5+3,sqrt(9));
right: select * from t where a>3;
label: invalid
note: Compares a scalar with a three-column row: an error in PostgreSQL and DuckDB.

left: select * from t where -a=3;
right: select * from t where a=-3;
label: equivalent

left: select a from t group by a having a>0;
right: select a from t where a>0 group by a;
label: equivalent
note: A HAVING condition on a grouping column moves to WHERE.

left: select sum(degree), sno, cno from score group by sno, cno having sum(degree)>100 and cno>0;
right: select sum(degree), sno, cno from score where cno>0 group by sno, cno having sum(degree)>100;
label: equivalent

left: select * from student where sname like 'abc%';
right: select * from student where sname>'abc' and sname<'abd';
label: not_equivalent
note: 'abc' itself matches LIKE 'abc%' but is not > 'abc' (and 'abd...' collation aside).

left: select * from student where sname like 'abc';
right: select * from student where sname='abc';
label: equivalent
note: A pattern without wildcards is an equality.

left: select * from student where sno between 10 and 20;
right: select * from student where sno>=10 and sno<=20;
label: equivalent

left: select * from student where not(sno!=10);
right: select * from student where sno=10;
label: equivalent
note: In WHERE, NOT(NULL) and NULL both drop the row.

left: select * from t where not(a!=b);
right: select * from t where a=b;
label: equivalent

left: select * from t where not(a=b);
right: select * from t where a!=b;
label: equivalent

left: select * from t where not(a<b);
right: select * from t where a>=b;
label: equivalent

left: select * from t where not(a>b);
right: select * from t where a<=b;
label: equivalent

left: select * from t1,t2 where t1.a>t2.b and t2.b>2;
right: select * from t1,t2 where t1.a>t2.b and t2.b>2 and t1.a>2;
label: equivalent
note: t1.a > t2.b > 2 implies t1.a > 2.

left: select * from t1, t2 where t1.a=1 and t1.a=t2.b;
right: select * from t1, t2 where t1.a=1 and t2.b=1;
label: equivalent

left: select * from t1, (select * from t2 ) sub_t2 where a=1 and sub_t2.b=a;
right: select * from t1, (select * from t2 where b=1 ) sub_t2 where a=1;
label: equivalent
note: a is t1.a (t2 has no column a); a = 1 and b = a give b = 1.

left: select distinct(sno) from student;
right: select sno from student;
label: equivalent
note: sno is the primary key.
adapted: the leading DDL fragment moved into the case's schema

left: select * from student where name is null and age>18;
right: select * from student where false;
label: equivalent
note: name is NOT NULL; the source DDL omits age, added here.
adapted: the leading DDL fragment moved into the case's schema

left: select * from t1 full join t2 on t1.a=t2.a where t1.b>5 and t2.c<10;
right: select * from t1 inner join t2 on t1.a=t2.a where t1.b>5 and t2.c<10;
label: equivalent
note: Both WHERE conditions reject the NULL-extended rows of the FULL JOIN.

left: select * from student where sno in (10,20,30);
right: select * from student where sno=10 or sno=20 or sno=30;
label: equivalent

left: select * from t1 where a1<10 and (exists (select a2 from t2 where t2.b2=1) or exists (select a2 from t2 where t2.b2=2 ));
right: select * from t1 where a1<10 and (exists (select a2 from t2 where t2.b2=1 or t2.b2=2));
label: equivalent

left: select * from student where (sex='f' and sno>15) or age>18;
right: select * from student where (sex='f' and sno>15) union all select * from student where age>18;
label: not_equivalent
note: A row matching both conditions appears once on the left and twice on the right.

left: select * from t1, (select * from t2 where t2.a2>10) v_t2 where t1.a1<10 and v_t2.a2<20;
right: select * from t1,t2 where t1.a1<10 and t2.a2<20 and t2.a2>10;
label: equivalent

left: select * from t1 where c1>(select max(t2.c2) from t2 where t2.c1=t1.c1)
right: select t1.* from t1 join (select t2.c1 t2_c1, max(t2.c2) max_t2_c2 from t2 group by t2.c1) as g on t1.c1=t2_c1 where t1.c1>max_t2_c2
label: equivalent
note: The source writes tc.c1 for t2.c1 (no table tc); scored with the typo fixed. Groups with no t2 row compare with NULL on the left and have no join row on the right.
adapted: tc.c1 read as t2.c1; the derived table gets an alias (PostgreSQL before 16 requires one)

left: select a, c from t1 where t1.a=(select avg(a) from t3 where t1.b=t3.b) or exists (select * from t4 where t1.c=t4.c)
right: select a, c from t1 left join (select avg(a) avg, t3.b from t3 group by t3.b) as t3 on (t1.a=avg and t1.b=t3.b) left join (select t4.c from t4 group by t4.c) where t3.b is not null or t4.c is not null;
label: invalid
note: The second LEFT JOIN has no ON condition.

left: select (select c2 from t2 where t1.c1=t2.c1) ssq, t1.c2 from t1 where t1.c2>10;
right: with ssq as (select t2.c2 from t2) select ssq.c2, t1.c2 from t1 left join ssq on t1.c1=ssq.c2 where t1.c2>10;
label: not_equivalent
note: The rewrite joins t1.c1 to t2.c2 instead of correlating on c1, and a scalar subquery returning several rows is an error on the left.

left: select (select count(*) from t2 where t2.c1=t1.c1) cnt, t1.c1, t3.c1 from t1,t3 where t1.c1=t3.c1 order by cnt, t1.c1;
right: with ssq as (select count(*) cnt, c1 from t2 group by c1) select case when ssq.cnt is null then 0 else ssq.cnt end cnt, t1.c1, t3.c1 from t1 left join ssq on ssq.c1=t1.c1,t3 where t1.c1=t3.c1 order by ssq.cnt, t1.c1;
label: equivalent
note: Equal as bags: a missing count is 0 on both sides. The ORDER BY differs (ssq.cnt is NULL where cnt is 0), so the row order can differ; KumoSQL compares bags.

left: select t1.c1, t1.c2 from t1 where t1.c1=(select agg() from t2.c2>t1.c2);
right: with dt as (select t1.rowid, agg() aggref from t1,t2 where t1.c2>t2.c2 group by t1.rowid) select t1.c1, t1.c2 from t1, derived_table where t1.rowid=derived_table.rowid AND t1.c1=derived_table.aggref;
label: invalid
note: agg() is a placeholder and "from t2.c2>t1.c2" is not SQL.
